scope: Shared native acceptance inputs and required outcomes. Fixture existence and Node reference checks are not runtime acceptance. No v4 app integration or increased caps.

currentStage.metadata: Complete bounded schema3 metadata/domain arrays, with receipt descriptors separated from raw payloads. This is not incremental metadata parsing.
currentStage.receiptInput: Supply one original receipt at a time from decoded fixture attachment dataBase64; candidate storage must not accumulate a second inline receipt graph. Keep exact original bytes.
currentStage.installation: A separately reviewed internal synchronous local install seam may consume only its own opaque finished candidate through the existing guarded publication/recovery path. Installation scenarios require fresh platform evidence; preparation evidence alone proves none of them. No cloud/provider or v4 archive integration.

invalidImageReference.instruction: Use exact public dataBase64 and recomputed/declared descriptor length/hash; retain replacement receipt and owner IDs. PNG chunk CRCs are valid, scanline filter is invalid.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Prepare replacement metadata and supply its raw receipt while previous is active; inspect before finish and after finish.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Previous identity, revision/incarnation, authenticated state digest, key identity and visible domains remain unchanged; finish returns only an inactive owned candidate.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Finish replacement and use only an internal test-authenticated inactive-candidate reopen to inspect its metadata and receipt bytes.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: All eight represented domain arrays and receipt original bytes match replacement, with no active install and no forgeable public installation capability.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Finish replacement, satisfy captured current identity guards, install and reopen from durable storage.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: All eight domain arrays equal replacement values, and receipt bytes equal the referenced original. Only documented local revision/incarnation metadata may change.
assertions: Keep previous active throughout receipt preparation/finish; install replacement through the same owning store only after all captured guards match.

Authenticate candidate catalog, metadata, complete receipt inventory, pinned file identity and native image bytes before publication; do not hydrate a new inline receipt graph merely to enter installation.

After successful guarded install, close candidate/old preparation owners and reopen a fresh store; compare exact fixture arrays, incoming vault/snapshot IDs and receipt bytes, plus documented local revision/incarnation changes.

Exercise duplicate/foreign-owner install, unavailable/changed current key, cancellation immediately before publication and failures at existing publication/verification checkpoints. Apply installationContract ownership and platform outcome rules; report each exercised boundary separately.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Substitute a receipt owner absent from replacement expenses, or substitute the expected owner while retaining the original descriptor binding.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Reject; no successful candidate/install, current remains previous.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Change one original byte without changing its declared SHA-256.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Reject; discard only owned candidate data.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Declare the replacement receipt but finish before supplying it.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Reject incomplete receipt inventory; no candidate success.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Supply the same receipt twice, or duplicate its descriptor ID.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Reject rather than replace or double-count the first receipt.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Supply a malformed image with recomputed length/hash and otherwise valid ownership. Reuse the native-invalid PNG corpus case named below.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Actual native image validation rejects before candidate success; hash agreement alone is insufficient.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Cancel before input and during a receipt read/write.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Reject and clean owned staging; current data/key unchanged.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Cancel before finish and at final validation/close completion boundaries.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Reject before inactive candidate transfer; no late successful handle after cancellation.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Inject read failure after partial bytes, and a source close failure after all expected bytes.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Neither failure is successful input; no candidate success and owned staging cleaned.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Inject encrypted-file write/sync/close/reopen failure, including failure at final finish.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Reject without exposing a successful candidate or deleting current/foreign data.

requiredScenarios.trigger: After success, failure and explicit discard, attempt more input, another finish and handle reuse. Exercise repeated discard/close separately.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Input/finish/reuse cannot revive the consumed operation. Cleanup is idempotent or explicitly rejects without touching another owner; transferred ownership cannot be reclaimed by the old operation.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Retain finished inactive candidate, perform an ordinary current-vault write and ordinary GC, then internally reopen candidate and finally discard it.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Pinned candidate data survives; ordinary current data remains authoritative. Discard releases only candidate ownership and later candidate reuse rejects.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Finish candidate; perform an ordinary active-vault edit through another instance; run ordinary GC while the candidate remains retained; try its original guarded install.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Candidate-owned rows/blobs remain readable while pinned, but install rejects stale current identity. The ordinary edit stays active; discard releases candidate ownership only.
assertions: Finish against previous; edit through another store instance and run ordinary GC while the candidate remains retained.
Prove candidate metadata and exact receipt bytes still authenticate while pinned, then attempt installation with the original captured binding.
Reject stale digest/revision/binding under the publication lease even if this instance cached previous; reopen and prove the ordinary edit remains active.
Reject subsequent handle reuse; close/discard removes only owned inactive data and preserves edited current data plus unknown/replaced entries.

requiredScenarios.trigger: After candidate finish, restore/recreate current state so a numeric revision repeats under a new incarnation, then install the old candidate.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Reject using authenticated state/incarnation guards; numeric revision equality is insufficient.
assertions: Finish candidate, then perform an independently valid restore/recreation that repeats a numeric revision under a new authenticated incarnation/state binding.
Install rejects despite revision equality; it cannot refresh its captured source digest/owner/key binding from current state or derive authority from candidate fixture IDs.
Reopen and verify the intervening state remains active; rejected handle reuse and cleanup preserve current and unknown/replaced entries.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Abort during partial input and after finish using the candidate owner; preserve current files and a deliberately unknown sibling/replaced pathname.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Delete only owned inactive candidate data. Never delete current or unknown/replaced entries; a consumed preparation owner cannot delete transferred candidate data.

requiredScenarios.trigger: Preview/prepare against an established vault whose device key lookup fails; instrument provisioning APIs.
requiredScenarios.requiredOutcome: Reject/lock, with zero key-provisioning calls and no empty-vault initialization or replacement of existing key/data.

futureSeparateGates: Incremental metadata parsing and larger-capacity admission
v4 record grammar, authenticated FINAL and strict EOF before candidate success
Provider/account/session/revision guards and exact downloaded-input binding when a provider reader is linked
Actual crash/fresh-process recovery and atomic-install evidence for this newly wired candidate entry point; ordinary in-process injection is not equivalent.
evidenceRequirements: Each native report records manifest SHA-256, source/build/runtime identity, exact test methods and per-scenario outcome.
Any omitted, skipped or not-yet-wired scenario includes its reason and remains unproved.
Prove single-use ownership, input close/cancel boundaries, current identity and native image validation on actual runtime; no filesystem simulation acceptance.

targetBinding.shared: Capture the receiving store and durable namespace identity, authenticated current-state digest/binding, current revision/incarnation and device-key identity before preparation. Revalidate under the same exclusive publication lease immediately before install. Re-read the current device key without provisioning. Candidate handles are one-shot and same-owner; fixture/public metadata cannot construct installation authority.
targetBinding.ios: Capture real directory/inode, sourceStoreId, sourceDigest, writerId, revision, restoreEpoch and key identity. Use fresh deviceKeyReader(false); derive the next local metadata internally and preserve the existing publication/rollback/reopen helper.
targetBinding.android: Capture owning store/database, activeState token, active generation/revision/incarnation, restoreBinding, verified source digest/vault and key-envelope identity. No new cloud writer setting is required. Authenticate owned catalog2 bytes/pinned files; catalog2-to-1 conversion and active-pointer publication occur in the same existing replacement transaction.

requiredAssertions: Install preserves replacement vaultId, snapshotId, all eight represented domain arrays and exact original receipt bytes; only platform-local revision/incarnation metadata changes according to the existing restore rule.
A failed current-key lookup or changed key identity before publication rejects/locks without provisioning, key-envelope replacement, empty initialization or current-data deletion.

Cancellation accepted before publication, stale identity and prepublication read/write/close/authentication failures never activate candidate bytes. The attempt cannot be retried with the consumed handle; owned inactive cleanup preserves current and unknown/replaced data.
Success transfers durable ownership: closing the candidate or former preparation operation cannot delete newly active or predecessor data. Duplicate install/input/finish/reuse rejects.

After publication, cancellation/failure follows the existing platform recovery boundary. Return success only for an authenticated settled replacement; confirmed rollback may report failure with previous preserved. An uncertain outcome retains potentially referenced bytes and locks/requires recovery; never claim previous kept without verifying rollback.

Candidate close/discard is idempotent or explicitly rejects without touching another owner. Retained pins protect candidate files until successful ownership transfer or safe owned cleanup; garbage collection must not decide install freshness.

platformCancellation.ios: Existing cancellation-aware publication uses noncancellable rollback I/O. Confirm rollback before discarding candidate ownership; retain bytes after successful or uncertain publication.
platformCancellation.android: RestoreOperation.beginPublication is the cancellation boundary. An accepted pre-CAS cancel rejects; after CAS, cancellation cannot claim old-vault retention and existing recover owns the settled result. Post-CAS/uncertain cleanup releases handles without deleting possibly published bytes.

installationContract.evidence: Report each assertion as executed, failed or not_run with reason and exact method/checkpoint. Failure injection is not process-death or physical power-loss proof; existing durable tests do not automatically establish the new candidate entry point.
